\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The problem}
Compression algorithms in the wild are \emph{universal}: a single decompressor is shipped once and must invert the compressor on every input it may meet. If the data were known to be drawn from a specific source $p$, the optimal code would spend $\log_2(1/p(x))$ bits on the message $x$. A universal scheme knows only that $p$ belongs to a class $\{p_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta}$. The question answered here is:

\begin{quote}
How many bits must a single universal code lose, in the worst case over messages and sources, relative to the code tailored to the true source?
\end{quote}

We call this the \emph{price of universality} of the class. It is the exact number of bits per message that a specialised scheme can save and a universal one cannot.

\subsection{Contributions}
\begin{enumerate}
\item An exact answer: the minimax pointwise redundancy is $\log_2\CS$, attained to within one bit by the NML code and unavoidable by every Kraft-compliant code (Section~\ref{sec:minimax}).
\item Closed-form upper bounds for memoryless and first-order Markov classes via a sufficient-statistic principle and a product-form counting bound (Section~\ref{sec:upper}).
\item A matching lower bound with explicit constants for the binary memoryless class: $\CS\ge\sqrt n/4$, price $\ge\tfrac12\log_2 n-2$ bits (Section~\ref{sec:lower}).
\item A separation theorem: on $n$-bit files the memoryless class costs $\Theta(\log n)$ bits while the class of point masses costs exactly $n$ bits (Section~\ref{sec:separation}).
\item Structural laws: calibration, monotonicity, exact multiplicativity over independent products, submultiplicativity under a shared parameter, and subadditivity of the memoryless price in block length (Section~\ref{sec:structure}).
\item The average-case dual: compensation identity, Bayes optimality of the mixture, the redundancy--capacity bound, and $I(w)\le\log_2\CS$ (Section~\ref{sec:capacity}).
\item Exact rational evidence at $n=2,4,8$ (Section~\ref{sec:evidence}).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Relation to classical theory}
The identification of the minimax pointwise redundancy with $\log_2\CS$ and the optimality of NML are due to Shtarkov; the $(d/2)\log_2 n$ redundancy rate for $d$-parameter families is due to Rissanen; the redundancy--capacity correspondence belongs to the Davisson--Gallager circle of ideas. The contribution here is a self-contained, constant-explicit development for finite message spaces, together with the separation theorem and the structural calculus.

\section{Setting and definitions}

Throughout, $X$ is a finite non-empty set of \emph{messages} and $\Theta$ a non-empty index set of \emph{sources}.

\begin{definition}[Source class]
A \emph{source class} on $X$ indexed by $\Theta$ is a family $p:\Theta\times X\to\mathbb R$ with $p_\theta(x)\ge0$ and $\sum_{x\in X}p_\theta(x)=1$ for all $\theta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Envelope, Shtarkov sum, NML]
\[
\phat(x)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}p_\theta(x),\qquad
\CS=\sum_{x\in X}\phat(x),\qquad
\qstar(x)=\frac{\phat(x)}{\CS}.
\]
The supremum exists since $p_\theta(x)\le1$. We call $\CS$ the \emph{Shtarkov sum} and $\qstar$ the \emph{normalized maximum likelihood} distribution.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Codes]
A \emph{length function} $\ell:X\to\mathbb N$ is \emph{Kraft compliant} if $\sum_{x}2^{-\ell(x)}\le1$; this is exactly the condition for a prefix-free binary code with those lengths to exist. The \emph{pointwise redundancy} of $\ell$ at $(\theta,x)$ with $p_\theta(x)>0$ is $\ell(x)-\log_2(1/p_\theta(x))$, and the \emph{price of universality} of the class is $\inf_\ell\sup_{\theta,x}\big(\ell(x)-\log_2(1/p_\theta(x))\big)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:basic}
$1\le\CS$, and if $\Theta$ is finite then $\CS\le|\Theta|$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Fix $\theta_0$; then $1=\sum_xp_{\theta_0}(x)\le\sum_x\phat(x)=\CS$. Conversely $\phat(x)\le\sum_\theta p_\theta(x)$ by non-negativity; summing over $x$ and exchanging sums gives $\CS\le|\Theta|$.
\end{proof}

Universality never helps, and never costs more than naming the source outright.

\section{The exact minimax theorem}\label{sec:minimax}

\begin{theorem}[NML dominates the class]\label{thm:dominate}
For every $\theta$ and $x$, $\ p_\theta(x)\le\CS\,\qstar(x)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\CS\qstar(x)=\phat(x)\ge p_\theta(x)$, and $\CS>0$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:basic}.
\end{proof}

Since $\sum_x\qstar(x)=1$, the code $\ell^\star(x)=\lceil\log_2(1/\qstar(x))\rceil$ satisfies $2^{-\ell^\star(x)}\le\qstar(x)$ termwise and is therefore Kraft compliant.

\begin{theorem}[Achievability in code lengths]\label{thm:achieve}
Assume $\phat(x)>0$ for all $x$. Then for every source $\theta$ and message $x$ with $p_\theta(x)>0$,
\[
\ell^\star(x)\ \le\ \log_2\frac{1}{p_\theta(x)}+\log_2\CS+1 .
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:dominate}, $1/\qstar(x)\le \CS/p_\theta(x)$, hence $\log_2(1/\qstar(x))\le\log_2(1/p_\theta(x))+\log_2\CS$. As $\qstar(x)\le1$, the quantity $\log_2(1/\qstar(x))$ is non-negative and its ceiling is less than itself plus one.
\end{proof}

A \emph{single} code, fixed in advance, is thus within $\log_2\CS+1$ bits of the ideal code for the true source, simultaneously for all sources and all messages.

\begin{theorem}[Converse]\label{thm:converse}
Let $q:X\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $\sum_xq(x)\le1$. Then there is $x$ with $q(x)\CS\le\phat(x)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Otherwise $\phat(x)<q(x)\CS$ for all $x$; summing the strict inequality over the non-empty finite set $X$ gives $\CS<(\sum_xq(x))\CS\le\CS$, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Kraft converse]\label{thm:kraft}
Let $\ell$ be Kraft compliant, $\Theta$ finite and all $p_\theta(x)>0$. Then there exist $x$ and $\theta$ with
\[
\ell(x)\ \ge\ \log_2\frac{1}{p_\theta(x)}+\log_2\CS .
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:converse} to the sub-probability $q(x)=2^{-\ell(x)}$; since $\Theta$ is finite the supremum $\phat(x)$ is attained at some $\theta$. Take logarithms in $\CS\le2^{\ell(x)}p_\theta(x)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Exact minimax redundancy]\label{thm:minimax}
For a source class with Shtarkov sum $\CS$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $p_\theta(x)\le\CS\,\qstar(x)$ for all $\theta,x$;
\item if $q\ge0$ satisfies $\sum_xq(x)\le1$ and $c\in\mathbb R$ satisfies $p_\theta(x)\le c\,q(x)$ for all $\theta,x$, then $\CS\le c$.
\end{enumerate}
Hence $\CS$ is the least constant of uniform domination of the class by a coding sub-probability, and $\log_2\CS$ is the minimax pointwise redundancy.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
(1) is Theorem~\ref{thm:dominate}. For (2), $p_\theta(x)\le cq(x)$ for all $\theta$ gives $\phat(x)\le cq(x)$; summing, $\CS\le c\sum_xq(x)$. Since $\CS\ge1>0$ we must have $c>0$, and then $c\sum_xq(x)\le c$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Mutually singular sources]\label{thm:singular}
If $\Theta$ is finite and there are pairwise disjoint $S_\theta\subseteq X$ with $\sum_{x\in S_\theta}p_\theta(x)=1$ for each $\theta$, then $\CS=|\Theta|$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
``$\le$'' is Proposition~\ref{prop:basic}. Conversely $|\Theta|=\sum_\theta\sum_{x\in S_\theta}p_\theta(x)\le\sum_\theta\sum_{x\in S_\theta}\phat(x)$, which by disjointness is a sum of $\phat$ over a subset of $X$, hence at most $\CS$.
\end{proof}

\section{Upper bounds: parametric classes cost only $O(\log n)$}\label{sec:upper}

\begin{theorem}[Sufficient-statistic bound]\label{thm:suffstat}
Let $T:X\to\sigma$ with $\sigma$ finite, and suppose $T(x)=T(y)$ implies $p_\theta(x)=p_\theta(y)$ for every $\theta$. Then $\CS\le|\sigma|$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Fix $s$, let $F=T^{-1}(s)$ and $k=|F|$. If $F=\emptyset$ its contribution vanishes. Otherwise $\phat$ is constant on $F$, say $=M$. For each $\theta$ and $x\in F$, $k\,p_\theta(x)=\sum_{y\in F}p_\theta(y)\le1$, so $p_\theta(x)\le1/k$; taking suprema, $M\le1/k$ and $\sum_{x\in F}\phat(x)=kM\le1$. The fibres partition $X$, and there are $|\sigma|$ of them.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Product-form counting bound]\label{thm:product}
Suppose $x$ determines features $b_1(x),\dots,b_m(x)\in B$ and an initial value $c(x)\in C$ with $B,C$ finite, and
\[
p_\theta(x)=h_\theta(c(x))\prod_{j=1}^{m}g_\theta(b_j(x)).
\]
Then $\CS\le|C|\,(m+1)^{|B|}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\prod_jg_\theta(b_j(x))=\prod_{b\in B}g_\theta(b)^{N_b(x)}$ with $N_b(x)=\#\{j:b_j(x)=b\}$, so the likelihood depends on $x$ only through $(c(x),(N_b(x))_{b\in B})$, a statistic with at most $|C|(m+1)^{|B|}$ values. Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:suffstat}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Memoryless sources}
Let $\Delta(A)=\{\theta:A\to[0,\infty):\sum_a\theta(a)=1\}$ and, on $X=A^n$, $p_\theta(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n\theta(x_i)$. These are probability distributions by the multinomial expansion of $(\sum_a\theta(a))^n=1$.

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:iid}
$\CS\le(n+1)^{|A|}$ for the memoryless class of block length $n$ over $A$. For $A=\{0,1\}$ the sharper bound $\CS\le n+1$ holds.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The first claim is Theorem~\ref{thm:product} with $B=A$, $m=n$, $|C|=1$, $g_\theta=\theta$, $h_\theta\equiv1$. For the binary case, the likelihood $\theta(1)^k\theta(0)^{n-k}$ depends on $x$ only through the number $k$ of ones, a statistic with $n+1$ values; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:suffstat} directly.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Bit-level guarantee]\label{thm:iidbits}
The NML code of the memoryless class satisfies, for every $\theta\in\Delta(A)$ and $x\in A^n$ with $p_\theta(x)>0$,
\[
\ell^\star(x)\ \le\ \log_2\frac{1}{p_\theta(x)}+|A|\log_2(n+1)+1 .
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:achieve} with $\log_2\CS\le|A|\log_2(n+1)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:iid}; the hypothesis $\phat>0$ holds because the uniform parameter gives every message positive probability.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Vanishing per-symbol price]\label{cor:rate}
For any constant $c$, $\big(c\log_2(n+1)+1\big)/n\to0$. A decompressor specialised to a memoryless class absorbs only a vanishing fraction of the message.
\end{corollary}

\subsection{First-order Markov sources}
Let the parameter be a pair $(\nu,T)$ of an initial law and a stochastic kernel, and on $X=A^{n+1}$ set $p_{(\nu,T)}(x)=\nu(x_0)\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}T(x_j,x_{j+1})$.

\begin{proposition}[Normalisation]\label{prop:markovnorm}
$\sum_{x\in A^{n+1}}p_{(\nu,T)}(x)=1$ for every probability vector $\nu$ and stochastic kernel $T$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Induction on $n$. For $n=0$ the sum is $\sum_a\nu(a)=1$. For the step, split off the first symbol:
\[
\sum_{x\in A^{n+2}}\nu(x_0)\!\!\prod_{j<n+1}\!\!T(x_j,x_{j+1})
=\sum_{y\in A^{n+1}}\Big(\sum_a\nu(a)T(a,y_0)\Big)\prod_{i<n}T(y_i,y_{i+1}),
\]
and $\nu'(b)=\sum_a\nu(a)T(a,b)$ is again a probability vector, since $\sum_b\nu'(b)=\sum_a\nu(a)=1$. Apply the induction hypothesis to $\nu'$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Markov redundancy]\label{thm:markov}
For the first-order Markov class on $A^{n+1}$,
\[
\CS\ \le\ |A|\,(n+1)^{|A|^2},
\]
and the NML code satisfies $\ell^\star(x)\le\log_2(1/p_\theta(x))+\log_2|A|+|A|^2\log_2(n+1)+1$ for every chain $\theta$ and message $x$ of positive probability.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:product} with feature alphabet $B=A\times A$ (the $n$ transition pairs), initial alphabet $C=A$, $g_\theta(a,b)=T(a,b)$ and $h_\theta(a)=\nu(a)$, so that $|B|=|A|^2$. The bit form follows from Theorem~\ref{thm:achieve}, the positivity hypothesis being witnessed by the uniform chain.
\end{proof}

The price is logarithmic in the message length, with the number of free parameters as the multiplier of $\log_2 n$: $|A|$ for memoryless sources, $|A|^2$ for first-order chains.

\section{The matching lower bound: the Rissanen floor}\label{sec:lower}

The class is binary memoryless on $X=\{0,1\}^n$; $k$ denotes the number of ones and $j=n-k$.

\begin{lemma}[Type fibres]\label{lem:fibre}
The set of binary strings of length $n$ with exactly $k$ ones has $\binom{n}{k}$ elements.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Maximum likelihood of a string]\label{lem:ml}
For a string $x$ with $k$ ones, the empirical parameter $\theta(1)=k/n$ maximises the likelihood, and
\[
\phat(x)\ \ge\ \Big(\frac kn\Big)^{k}\Big(\frac{n-k}{n}\Big)^{n-k}
\]
(with equality, and with the convention $0^0=1$).
\end{lemma}

Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:CSformula}
\CS=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\binom{n}{k}\Big(\frac kn\Big)^{k}\Big(\frac{n-k}{n}\Big)^{n-k}.
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[Stirling, upper]\label{lem:stirup}
For $m\ge1$, $\ m!\le e\sqrt m\,(m/e)^m$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The Stirling sequence $s_m=m!/(\sqrt{2m}\,(m/e)^m)$ is antitone for $m\ge1$, so $s_m\le s_1=e/\sqrt2$; rearranging gives the claim.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Stirling, lower]\label{lem:stirlow}
$\sqrt{2\pi m}\,(m/e)^m\le m!$ for all $m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Every interior type is heavy]\label{thm:typeterm}
Let $k,j\ge1$ and $n=k+j$. Then
\[
\binom{n}{k}\Big(\frac kn\Big)^{k}\Big(\frac jn\Big)^{j}\ \ge\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt n}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Since $(k/n)^k(j/n)^j=(k/e)^k(j/e)^j/(n/e)^n$ (the powers of $e$ and of $n$ cancel because $k+j=n$), the left-hand side equals
\[
\frac{n!}{(n/e)^n}\cdot\frac{(k/e)^k}{k!}\cdot\frac{(j/e)^j}{j!} .
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:stirlow} the first factor is at least $\sqrt{2\pi n}$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:stirup} the second and third are at least $1/(e\sqrt k)$ and $1/(e\sqrt j)$. Hence the product is at least $\sqrt{2\pi n}/(e^2\sqrt{kj})$. Now $\sqrt{kj}\le n/2$ by AM--GM, and $\sqrt{2\pi}>2.5$, $e^2<7.4$, so the bound is at least $(2.5\sqrt n)/(7.4\,n/2)=(5/7.4)/\sqrt n\ge1/(2\sqrt n)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound on the Shtarkov sum]\label{thm:sqrtlower}
For $n\ge2$, the binary memoryless class satisfies $\CS\ge\sqrt n/4$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The type fibres $F_k$ are pairwise disjoint, and by Lemmas~\ref{lem:fibre},~\ref{lem:ml} and Theorem~\ref{thm:typeterm}, for $1\le k\le n-1$,
\[
\sum_{x\in F_k}\phat(x)\ \ge\ \binom nk\Big(\frac kn\Big)^k\Big(\frac{n-k}{n}\Big)^{n-k}\ \ge\ \frac{1}{2\sqrt n}.
\]
Summing over the $n-1$ interior types and discarding the two extreme (non-negative) types, $\CS\ge(n-1)/(2\sqrt n)\ge\sqrt n/4$, the last step being $4(n-1)\ge2n$, i.e.\ $n\ge2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Sandwich]\label{thm:sandwich}
For $n\ge2$,
\[
\tfrac12\log_2 n-2\ \le\ \log_2\CS\ \le\ \log_2(n+1).
\]
Equivalently, every Kraft-compliant code has a message and a Bernoulli source on which it exceeds the ideal code length by at least $\tfrac12\log_2 n-2$ bits, while the NML code never exceeds it by more than $\log_2(n+1)+1$ bits.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Lower bound: Theorem~\ref{thm:sqrtlower} with $\log_2(\sqrt n/4)=\tfrac12\log_2 n-2$, combined with Theorem~\ref{thm:kraft}. Upper bound: Theorem~\ref{thm:iid} combined with Theorem~\ref{thm:achieve}.
\end{proof}

The lower bound is exactly the Rissanen rate $(d/2)\log_2 n$ at $d=1$, so the theory is not an upper-bound artefact; the two sides agree to within a factor of two and an additive constant.

\section{Separation: when specialisation buys nothing}\label{sec:separation}

\begin{definition}[Deterministic class]
For finite $X$, the \emph{deterministic class} is $\{\delta_y\}_{y\in X}$ with $\delta_y(x)=1$ if $x=y$ and $0$ otherwise: operationally, one decompressor per file.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:delta}
For the deterministic class, $\phat\equiv1$ and $\CS=|X|$ exactly. On $n$-bit files, $\log_2\CS=n$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\phat(x)\ge\delta_x(x)=1$ and $\phat(x)\le1$; sum the constant $1$ over $X$. Alternatively apply Theorem~\ref{thm:singular} with $S_y=\{y\}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Separation]\label{thm:separation}
On the message space of $n$-bit files with $n\ge2$,
\[
\tfrac12\log_2 n-2\ \le\ \log_2\CS^{\mathrm{memoryless}}\ \le\ \log_2(n+1),
\qquad
\log_2\CS^{\mathrm{deterministic}}=n,
\]
and $\log_2(n+1)/n\to0$.
\end{theorem}

Each specialist of the deterministic class saves all $n$ bits on its own file, and the universal scheme facing that class pays exactly $n$ bits: savings and price cancel identically, and \emph{no} bits move from the message into the shared decompressor. At the other extreme a one-parameter class transfers $\Theta(\log n)$ bits --- real, but a vanishing fraction of the file.

\section{Structural laws of the price}\label{sec:structure}

\begin{theorem}[Calibration]\label{thm:calib}
If all sources of the class have the same law, then $\CS=1$ and the price is exactly $0$ bits.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity]\label{thm:mono}
If $\iota:\Theta'\to\Theta$ is any reindexing (in particular a subclass inclusion), the Shtarkov sum of the reindexed class is at most that of the original.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Pointwise, $\sup_{\theta'}p_{\iota(\theta')}(x)\le\sup_\theta p_\theta(x)$; sum over $x$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Product classes]
The \emph{independent product} of classes $S_1$ on $X_1$ and $S_2$ on $X_2$ is indexed by $\Theta_1\times\Theta_2$ with $p_{(\theta_1,\theta_2)}(x_1,x_2)=p_{\theta_1}(x_1)p_{\theta_2}(x_2)$. The \emph{tied product} of two classes indexed by a common $\Theta$ is $p_\theta(x_1,x_2)=p^{(1)}_\theta(x_1)p^{(2)}_\theta(x_2)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact multiplicativity]\label{thm:mult}
For the independent product, $\CS=\CS^{(1)}\CS^{(2)}$; the price in bits is exactly additive.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The supremum of a product of non-negative functions over a product index set factorises, and the resulting double sum factors.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Submultiplicativity under sharing]\label{thm:tied}
For the tied product, $\CS\le\CS^{(1)}\CS^{(2)}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A single $\theta$ must serve both factors, so $\sup_\theta p^{(1)}_\theta(x_1)p^{(2)}_\theta(x_2)\le\phat^{(1)}(x_1)\phat^{(2)}(x_2)$; sum.
\end{proof}

These two theorems explain the whole paper: a class that re-chooses its parameter on each block pays additively (whence $n$ bits for the deterministic class), while a class sharing one parameter pays only subadditively, and the slack is exactly what turns a linear price into a logarithmic one.

\begin{corollary}[Subadditivity in block length]\label{cor:fekete}
For the memoryless class over a fixed alphabet, $\CS(n_1+n_2)\le\CS(n_1)\CS(n_2)$; hence $\log_2\CS(n)$ is subadditive and $\log_2\CS(n)/n$ converges by Fekete's lemma --- to $0$, by Corollary~\ref{cor:rate}.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Splitting a message of length $n_1+n_2$ into two blocks identifies the memoryless class with the tied product of the two shorter memoryless classes; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:tied}, using invariance of $\CS$ under bijective relabellings of the message space.
\end{proof}

\section{The average-case dual: redundancy as capacity}\label{sec:capacity}

Here $\Theta$ is finite, all $p_\theta(x)>0$, and $w$ is a strictly positive prior with $\sum_\theta w_\theta=1$.

\begin{definition}
For probability vectors with positive entries,
$\KL{p}{q}=\sum_xp(x)\log_2\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$ and $H(w)=-\sum_\theta w_\theta\log_2w_\theta$. The \emph{mixture} is $m_w(x)=\sum_\theta w_\theta p_\theta(x)$, the \emph{capacity functional} is $I(w)=\sum_\theta w_\theta\KL{p_\theta}{m_w}$, and the \emph{Bayes redundancy} of a coding distribution $q$ is $\bar R(w,q)=\sum_\theta w_\theta\KL{p_\theta}{q}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Gibbs]\label{thm:gibbs}
$\KL{p}{q}\ge0$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
With $\ln t\le t-1$ at $t=q(x)/p(x)$: $\sum_xp(x)\ln(q(x)/p(x))\le\sum_x(q(x)-p(x))=0$; divide by $-\ln2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Compensation identity]\label{thm:comp}
For every coding distribution $q$ with positive entries,
\[
\bar R(w,q)=I(w)+\KL{m_w}{q}.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Split $\log_2\frac{p_\theta(x)}{q(x)}=\log_2\frac{p_\theta(x)}{m_w(x)}+\log_2\frac{m_w(x)}{q(x)}$, multiply by $w_\theta p_\theta(x)$ and sum over $\theta$ and $x$. The first group gives $I(w)$; in the second the logarithm is independent of $\theta$, so summing $w_\theta p_\theta(x)$ over $\theta$ yields $m_w(x)$ and the remaining sum is $\KL{m_w}{q}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Bayes optimality of the mixture]\label{cor:bayes}
$I(w)\le\bar R(w,q)$ for every coding distribution $q$, with equality iff $q=m_w$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Redundancy--capacity lower bound]\label{thm:redcap}
For every coding distribution $q$ there is $\theta$ with $\KL{p_\theta}{q}\ge I(w)$; hence $\sup_wI(w)\le\inf_q\sup_\theta\KL{p_\theta}{q}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
If $\KL{p_\theta}{q}<I(w)$ for all $\theta$, averaging with the strictly positive weights gives $\bar R(w,q)<I(w)$, contradicting Corollary~\ref{cor:bayes}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Consistency with the worst-case theory]\label{thm:consistency}
If additionally $\phat(x)>0$ for all $x$, then $\KL{p_\theta}{\qstar}\le\log_2\CS$ for every $\theta$, and hence $I(w)\le\log_2\CS$ for every prior.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By Theorem~\ref{thm:dominate}, $p_\theta(x)/\qstar(x)\le\CS$ pointwise, so $\KL{p_\theta}{\qstar}\le\log_2\CS$. Apply Corollary~\ref{cor:bayes} with $q=\qstar$ and average.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Naming the source]\label{thm:naming}
$I(w)\le H(w)\le\log_2|\Theta|$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$m_w(x)\ge w_\theta p_\theta(x)$ gives $\KL{p_\theta}{m_w}\le-\log_2w_\theta$; average. The second inequality is the maximum-entropy property of the uniform prior.
\end{proof}

Both sides of Theorem~\ref{thm:sandwich} hold with room to spare, and $\CS$ is strictly increasing over the computed range --- inconsistent with any bounded-price conjecture and consistent with growth of order $\sqrt n$.

\section{Discussion}

\subsection{The answer to the design question}
For a class $\mathcal C$ of data:
\begin{itemize}
\item the maximum number of bits per message that specialisation can move out of the message and into the shared decompressor is exactly $\log_2\CS(\mathcal C)$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:minimax});
\item if $\mathcal C$ is parametric, that number is $\Theta(\log n)$ --- at least $\tfrac12\log_2 n-2$ and at most $\log_2(n+1)$ in the binary memoryless case (Theorem~\ref{thm:sandwich}), at most $|A|\log_2(n+1)$ and $\log_2|A|+|A|^2\log_2(n+1)$ for general memoryless and Markov classes (Theorems~\ref{thm:iidbits},~\ref{thm:markov});
\item if $\mathcal C$ can name individual files, that number is $n$ on $n$-bit files (Theorem~\ref{thm:delta}), and the specialists' savings are exactly cancelled;
\item the transition is governed by parameter sharing: additive without (Theorem~\ref{thm:mult}), subadditive with (Theorem~\ref{thm:tied}).
\end{itemize}
Hence: specialised decompressors are worth pursuing precisely when the data class is genuinely low-complexity relative to the data volume, and the benefit is at most logarithmic in that volume for any fixed parametric model.

\subsection{Sharpness and limitations}
The lower bound reproduces the classical parametric rate at dimension one with explicit constants and no asymptotics, and the upper bound for the same class is within a factor of two in the coefficient of $\log_2 n$. For higher-dimensional classes the upper bound $|A|\log_2(n+1)$ exceeds the expected $\frac{|A|-1}{2}\log_2 n$ by roughly a factor of two; closing the gap requires the multi-index analogue of Theorem~\ref{thm:typeterm}. All results concern finite message spaces and classes of probability distributions; algorithmic (Kolmogorov) universality is not treated, and the capacity theory is developed for strictly positive laws and priors.

\subsection{Practical readings}
The NML code of a parametric class is a single fixed code losing at most $\log_2\CS+1$ bits on \emph{every} message, which is why adaptive arithmetic coders with Krichevsky--Trofimov-style estimators --- close relatives of the mixture code, optimal on average by Corollary~\ref{cor:bayes} --- perform so well. The quantity $\log_2\CS$ is the parametric complexity term of the minimum description length principle, and Theorem~\ref{thm:suffstat} states precisely that only the number of distinguishable statistics matters. Shipping a large shared dictionary or pretrained model with a codec is the deterministic-class trade in disguise when the shared object is as expressive as the data: it pays only if its effective description length is small relative to the data it serves.

\section{Future work}

\paragraph{Full Rissanen rate for general alphabets.} For the memoryless class over an alphabet of size $a$ we conjecture $\log_2\CS=\frac{a-1}{2}\log_2 n+O(1)$, with constant $\log_2\big(\Gamma(1/2)^a/\Gamma(a/2)\big)+\frac{a-1}{2}\log_2(n/2\pi)$. The one-dimensional proof factorises: each interior type contributes $\prod_i\sqrt{n/(2\pi n_i)}$ by the same Stirling sandwich, and the sum over the $(a-1)$-dimensional type lattice is a Riemann sum for the Dirichlet$(\tfrac12,\dots,\tfrac12)$ normaliser.

\paragraph{Minimax equals maximin.} We conjecture $\sup_wI(w)=\inf_q\sup_\theta\KL{p_\theta}{q}$ for every finite class, both equal to $\log_2\CS$ up to $o(1)$ for smooth families; the compensation identity gives one inequality and the reverse is a minimax exchange on the compact simplex of priors.

\paragraph{Higher-order and finite-state sources.} The product-form bound gives $\CS\le|A|^r(n+1)^{|A|^{r+1}}$ for order-$r$ chains; matching lower bounds and the correct dependence on the state count remain open.

\paragraph{Sharpening the binary constants.} Replacing the discard of the extreme types and the AM--GM step by an exact Riemann-sum evaluation of \eqref{eq:CSformula} should give $\log_2\CS=\tfrac12\log_2 n+\tfrac12\log_2(\pi/2)+o(1)$.

\paragraph{The price as a functional on classes.} Which operations on classes are exactly multiplicative, and what is the price of a class defined by a constraint such as bounded entropy rate or bounded distance from a reference source?

def binomial(n: int, k: int) -> int:

    return math.comb(n, k)


def shtarkov_bernoulli_exact(n: int) -> Fraction:
    """Exact Shtarkov sum of the binary memoryless class on n-bit messages.

    C_S(n) = sum_{k=0}^{n} C(n,k) (k/n)^k ((n-k)/n)^(n-k),  with 0^0 = 1.

    Each string of length n with k ones has maximum likelihood
    (k/n)^k ((n-k)/n)^(n-k), attained at the empirical Bernoulli parameter,
    and there are C(n,k) such strings.
    """
    if n == 0:
        return Fraction(1)
    total = Fraction(0)
    for k in range(n + 1):
        p = Fraction(k, n)
        q = Fraction(n - k, n)
        total += binomial(n, k) * (p ** k) * (q ** (n - k))
    return total


def price_bits(c_s: Fraction) -> float:
    """Price of universality in bits, log2 of the Shtarkov sum."""
    return math.log2(float(c_s))

# 2.  Explicit source classes on a small message space
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

Message = Tuple[int, ...]


def all_messages(n: int) -> List[Message]:
    """All binary strings of length n, as tuples of 0/1."""
    return list(itertools.product((0, 1), repeat=n))


def bernoulli_likelihood(theta: float, x: Message) -> float:
    """p_theta(x) for a memoryless binary source with P(1) = theta."""
    k = sum(x)
    n = len(x)
    return (theta ** k) * ((1.0 - theta) ** (n - k))


def max_likelihood_envelope(messages: Sequence[Message],
                            likelihood: Callable[[float, Message], float],
                            params: Sequence[float]) -> Dict[Message, float]:
    """Pointwise envelope  x -> max_theta p_theta(x)  over a parameter grid."""
    return {x: max(likelihood(t, x) for t in params) for x in messages}


def bernoulli_envelope_exact(n: int) -> Dict[Message, float]:
    """Exact envelope for the binary memoryless class: the ML parameter of a
    string with k ones is k/n, so the envelope is (k/n)^k ((n-k)/n)^(n-k)."""
    out: Dict[Message, float] = {}
    for x in all_messages(n):
        k = sum(x)
        t = k / n
        out[x] = (t ** k) * ((1 - t) ** (n - k)) if 0 < k < n else 1.0
    return out


def nml_distribution(envelope: Dict[Message, float]) -> Dict[Message, float]:
    """Normalized maximum likelihood distribution q*(x) = envelope(x)/C_S."""
    c_s = sum(envelope.values())
    return {x: v / c_s for x, v in envelope.items()}


def nml_code_lengths(q_star: Dict[Message, float]) -> Dict[Message, int]:
    """Integer NML code lengths, ceil(log2 (1/q*(x)))."""
    return {x: math.ceil(math.log2(1.0 / q)) for x, q in q_star.items()}


def kraft_sum(lengths: Dict[Message, int]) -> float:
    """Kraft sum  sum_x 2^{-l(x)};  <= 1 iff a prefix-free code exists."""
    return sum(2.0 ** (-l) for l in lengths.values())


def nml_guarantee_report(n: int = 8, thetas: Iterable[float] = (0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8)) -> None:
    """Show that the single NML code is within log2 C_S + 1 bits of the ideal
    code of every source, on every message."""
    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"2.  The universal NML code on n = {n} bit messages")
    print("=" * 78)
    envelope = bernoulli_envelope_exact(n)
    c_s = sum(envelope.values())
    q_star = nml_distribution(envelope)
    lengths = nml_code_lengths(q_star)
    print(f"  C_S = {c_s:.6f}    log2 C_S = {math.log2(c_s):.4f} bits")
    print(f"  Kraft sum of the NML code: {kraft_sum(lengths):.6f}  (must be <= 1)")
    print(f"\n  {'theta':>6} {'max excess over ideal (bits)':>30} "
          f"{'bound log2 C_S + 1':>20}")
    worst_overall = 0.0
    for theta in thetas:
        worst = max(
            lengths[x] - math.log2(1.0 / bernoulli_likelihood(theta, x))
            for x in envelope
            if bernoulli_likelihood(theta, x) > 0
        )
        worst_overall = max(worst_overall, worst)
        print(f"  {theta:>6.2f} {worst:>30.4f} {math.log2(c_s)+1:>20.4f}")
    print(f"\n  worst excess over all tested sources and all messages: "
          f"{worst_overall:.4f} bits  <=  {math.log2(c_s)+1:.4f}: "
          f"{worst_overall <= math.log2(c_s) + 1 + 1e-12}")
    print()


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.  The converse: no code beats log2 C_S everywhere
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------


def converse_search(n: int = 4, trials: int = 20000, seed: int = 20260817) -> None:
    """Randomly probe Kraft-compliant codes and record the best achievable
    worst-case redundancy; the theory says it can never fall below log2 C_S."""
    import random

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    messages = all_messages(n)
    envelope = bernoulli_envelope_exact(n)
    c_s = sum(envelope.values())

    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"3.  Converse: random search over codes on n = {n} bit messages")
    print("=" * 78)

    def worst_case(q: Dict[Message, float]) -> float:
        """sup_x log2( max_theta p_theta(x) / q(x) ): the pointwise redundancy
        of the coding distribution q against the whole class."""
        return max(math.log2(envelope[x] / q[x]) for x in messages)

    best = float("inf")
    for _ in range(trials):
        # a random coding distribution, biased towards the envelope so that
        # the search actually gets close to the optimum
        weights = [envelope[x] ** rng.uniform(0.5, 1.5) * rng.random()
                   + 1e-12 for x in messages]
        total = sum(weights)
        q = {x: w / total for x, w in zip(messages, weights)}
        best = min(best, worst_case(q))

    q_star = nml_distribution(envelope)
    print(f"  log2 C_S (theoretical minimum of the worst case) = {math.log2(c_s):.6f}")
    print(f"  worst case of the NML distribution               = "
          f"{worst_case(q_star):.6f}   (attains the minimum)")
    print(f"  best worst case found in {trials} random codes        = {best:.6f}")
    print(f"  no random code beat the bound: {best >= math.log2(c_s) - 1e-9}")
    print()

# 5.  Structural laws: additivity and subadditivity
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------


def shtarkov_of_table(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> float:
    """C_S of a finite class given as a table probs[theta][x]."""
    n_msgs = len(probs[0])
    return sum(max(row[x] for row in probs) for x in range(n_msgs))


def product_class(p1: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
                  p2: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> List[List[float]]:
    """Independent product: parameters chosen separately in each block."""
    return [
        [a * b for a in row1 for b in row2]
        for row1 in p1
        for row2 in p2
    ]


def tied_product_class(p1: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
                       p2: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> List[List[float]]:
    """Tied product: one shared parameter drives both blocks."""
    assert len(p1) == len(p2)
    return [
        [a * b for a in p1[t] for b in p2[t]]
        for t in range(len(p1))
    ]

    c1, c2 = shtarkov_of_table(p1), shtarkov_of_table(p2)

    c_tied = shtarkov_of_table(tied_product_class(p1, p2))
    print(f"  block 1:  C_S = {c1:.6f}   price = {math.log2(c1):.4f} bits")
    print(f"  block 2:  C_S = {c2:.6f}   price = {math.log2(c2):.4f} bits")

# 6.  The average-case dual: capacity, mixture, compensation identity
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------


def kl_bits(p: Sequence[float], q: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Relative entropy in bits between two positive probability vectors."""
    return sum(pi * math.log2(pi / qi) for pi, qi in zip(p, q))


def mixture(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], w: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """Bayes mixture m_w(x) = sum_theta w_theta p_theta(x)."""
    n_msgs = len(probs[0])
    return [sum(w[t] * probs[t][x] for t in range(len(probs))) for x in range(n_msgs)]


def mutual_information(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], w: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Capacity functional I(w) = sum_theta w_theta D(p_theta || m_w), in bits."""
    m = mixture(probs, w)
    return sum(w[t] * kl_bits(probs[t], m) for t in range(len(probs)))


def bayes_redundancy(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], w: Sequence[float],
                     q: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Average redundancy sum_theta w_theta D(p_theta || q), in bits."""
    return sum(w[t] * kl_bits(probs[t], q) for t in range(len(probs)))


def capacity_report() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("6.  Average case: compensation identity and redundancy-capacity")
    print("=" * 78)
    probs = [
        [0.70, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10],
        [0.10, 0.70, 0.10, 0.10],
        [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25],
    ]
    w = [0.5, 0.3, 0.2]
    envelope = [max(row[x] for row in probs) for x in range(4)]
    c_s = sum(envelope)
    q_star = [e / c_s for e in envelope]
    m = mixture(probs, w)

    i_w = mutual_information(probs, w)
    print(f"  prior w = {w}")
    print(f"  capacity functional I(w)      = {i_w:.6f} bits")
    print(f"  worst-case price log2 C_S     = {math.log2(c_s):.6f} bits")
    print(f"  prior entropy H(w)            = "
          f"{-sum(wi*math.log2(wi) for wi in w):.6f} bits")
    print(f"  log2 |Theta|                  = {math.log2(len(probs)):.6f} bits")
    print(f"  I(w) <= log2 C_S : {i_w <= math.log2(c_s) + 1e-12}")

    print("\n  compensation identity  Rbar(w,q) = I(w) + D(m_w || q):")
    for name, q in (("mixture m_w", m), ("NML q*", q_star),
                    ("uniform", [0.25] * 4)):
        rbar = bayes_redundancy(probs, w, q)
        excess = kl_bits(m, q)
        print(f"    q = {name:<12}  Rbar = {rbar:.6f} = "
              f"I(w) {i_w:.6f} + D(m||q) {excess:.6f}  "
              f"[residual {abs(rbar - i_w - excess):.2e}]")
    print("\n  the mixture is Bayes optimal: no coding distribution has")
    print("  average redundancy below I(w).")
    print()

    return sum(2.0 ** (-l) for l in lengths.values())

    print(f"  C_S = {c_s:.6f}    log2 C_S = {math.log2(c_s):.4f} bits")

    print()

def converse_search(n: int = 4, trials: int = 20000, seed: int = 20260817) -> None:
    """Randomly probe Kraft-compliant codes and record the best achievable
    worst-case redundancy; the theory says it can never fall below log2 C_S."""
    import random

    rng = random.Random(seed)
    messages = all_messages(n)
    envelope = bernoulli_envelope_exact(n)
    c_s = sum(envelope.values())

    print("=" * 78)
    print(f"3.  Converse: random search over codes on n = {n} bit messages")
    print("=" * 78)

    def worst_case(q: Dict[Message, float]) -> float:
        """sup_x log2( max_theta p_theta(x) / q(x) ): the pointwise redundancy
        of the coding distribution q against the whole class."""
        return max(math.log2(envelope[x] / q[x]) for x in messages)

    best = float("inf")
    for _ in range(trials):
        # a random coding distribution, biased towards the envelope so that
        # the search actually gets close to the optimum
        weights = [envelope[x] ** rng.uniform(0.5, 1.5) * rng.random()
                   + 1e-12 for x in messages]
        total = sum(weights)
        q = {x: w / total for x, w in zip(messages, weights)}
        best = min(best, worst_case(q))

    q_star = nml_distribution(envelope)
    print(f"  log2 C_S (theoretical minimum of the worst case) = {math.log2(c_s):.6f}")
    print(f"  worst case of the NML distribution               = "
          f"{worst_case(q_star):.6f}   (attains the minimum)")
    print(f"  best worst case found in {trials} random codes        = {best:.6f}")
    print(f"  no random code beat the bound: {best >= math.log2(c_s) - 1e-9}")
    print()

def shtarkov_of_table(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> float:
    """C_S of a finite class given as a table probs[theta][x]."""
    n_msgs = len(probs[0])
    return sum(max(row[x] for row in probs) for x in range(n_msgs))


def product_class(p1: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
                  p2: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> List[List[float]]:
    """Independent product: parameters chosen separately in each block."""
    return [
        [a * b for a in row1 for b in row2]
        for row1 in p1
        for row2 in p2
    ]


def tied_product_class(p1: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
                       p2: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> List[List[float]]:
    """Tied product: one shared parameter drives both blocks."""
    assert len(p1) == len(p2)
    return [
        [a * b for a in p1[t] for b in p2[t]]
        for t in range(len(p1))
    ]

# 6.  The average-case dual: capacity, mixture, compensation identity

def kl_bits(p: Sequence[float], q: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Relative entropy in bits between two positive probability vectors."""
    return sum(pi * math.log2(pi / qi) for pi, qi in zip(p, q))


def mixture(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], w: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """Bayes mixture m_w(x) = sum_theta w_theta p_theta(x)."""
    n_msgs = len(probs[0])
    return [sum(w[t] * probs[t][x] for t in range(len(probs))) for x in range(n_msgs)]


def mutual_information(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], w: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Capacity functional I(w) = sum_theta w_theta D(p_theta || m_w), in bits."""
    m = mixture(probs, w)
    return sum(w[t] * kl_bits(probs[t], m) for t in range(len(probs)))


def bayes_redundancy(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], w: Sequence[float],
                     q: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Average redundancy sum_theta w_theta D(p_theta || q), in bits."""
    return sum(w[t] * kl_bits(probs[t], q) for t in range(len(probs)))


def capacity_report() -> None:
    print("=" * 78)
    print("6.  Average case: compensation identity and redundancy-capacity")
    print("=" * 78)
    probs = [
        [0.70, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10],

        [0.25, 0.25, 0.25, 0.25],

    w = [0.5, 0.3, 0.2]
    envelope = [max(row[x] for row in probs) for x in range(4)]
    c_s = sum(envelope)
    q_star = [e / c_s for e in envelope]
    m = mixture(probs, w)

    i_w = mutual_information(probs, w)
    print(f"  prior w = {w}")
    print(f"  capacity functional I(w)      = {i_w:.6f} bits")
    print(f"  worst-case price log2 C_S     = {math.log2(c_s):.6f} bits")
    print(f"  prior entropy H(w)            = "
          f"{-sum(wi*math.log2(wi) for wi in w):.6f} bits")
    print(f"  log2 |Theta|                  = {math.log2(len(probs)):.6f} bits")
    print(f"  I(w) <= log2 C_S : {i_w <= math.log2(c_s) + 1e-12}")

    print("\n  compensation identity  Rbar(w,q) = I(w) + D(m_w || q):")
    for name, q in (("mixture m_w", m), ("NML q*", q_star),
                    ("uniform", [0.25] * 4)):
        rbar = bayes_redundancy(probs, w, q)
        excess = kl_bits(m, q)
        print(f"    q = {name:<12}  Rbar = {rbar:.6f} = "
              f"I(w) {i_w:.6f} + D(m||q) {excess:.6f}  "
              f"[residual {abs(rbar - i_w - excess):.2e}]")
    print("\n  the mixture is Bayes optimal: no coding distribution has")
    print("  average redundancy below I(w).")
    print()

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple


def shtarkov_sum_bernoulli(n: int) -> Fraction:
    """Exact C_S(n) = sum_{k=0}^n C(n,k) (k/n)^k ((n-k)/n)^(n-k), with 0^0 = 1.

    Complexity: O(n) rational multiplications of numbers of O(n log n) bits,
    i.e. O~(n^2) bit operations -- versus O(2^n) for a naive sum over messages.
    """
    if n == 0:
        return Fraction(1)
    total = Fraction(0)
    for k in range(n + 1):
        total += (math.comb(n, k)
                  * Fraction(k, n) ** k
                  * Fraction(n - k, n) ** (n - k))
    return total


def price_of_universality_bits(n: int) -> float:
    """log2 C_S(n): the exact minimax pointwise redundancy, in bits."""
    return math.log2(float(shtarkov_sum_bernoulli(n)))


def nml_type_probabilities(n: int) -> List[Fraction]:
    """NML probability of each individual string, indexed by its type k.

    q*(x) = maxlik(x) / C_S, where maxlik depends only on k = #ones(x).
    """
    c_s = shtarkov_sum_bernoulli(n)
    out: List[Fraction] = []
    for k in range(n + 1):
        maxlik = Fraction(k, n) ** k * Fraction(n - k, n) ** (n - k) if n else Fraction(1)
        out.append(maxlik / c_s)
    return out


def nml_code_lengths(n: int) -> Dict[int, int]:
    """Integer NML code length ceil(log2 (1/q*(x))) for each type k.

    The resulting length function is Kraft compliant, hence realizable by a
    prefix-free code, and is within log2 C_S + 1 bits of the ideal code of the
    true Bernoulli source on every message.
    """
    return {k: math.ceil(-math.log2(float(q)))
            for k, q in enumerate(nml_type_probabilities(n))}


def kraft_sum(n: int) -> float:
    """sum_x 2^{-l*(x)} over all 2^n messages; must be <= 1."""
    lengths = nml_code_lengths(n)
    return sum(math.comb(n, k) * 2.0 ** (-lengths[k]) for k in range(n + 1))


def sandwich(n: int) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
    """(lower bound, exact price, upper bound) in bits, valid for n >= 2."""
    return (0.5 * math.log2(n) - 2.0, price_of_universality_bits(n),
            math.log2(n + 1))

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Iterator, List, Tuple


def compositions(total: int, parts: int) -> Iterator[Tuple[int, ...]]:
    """All non-negative integer tuples of the given length summing to `total`.

    There are C(total + parts - 1, parts - 1) of them; this is the type lattice
    of a memoryless class of block length `total` over an alphabet of size
    `parts`.
    """
    if parts == 1:
        yield (total,)
        return
    for first in range(total + 1):
        for rest in compositions(total - first, parts - 1):
            yield (first,) + rest


def multinomial(counts: Tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
    """Number of strings with the given symbol counts."""
    n = sum(counts)
    out = math.factorial(n)
    for c in counts:
        out //= math.factorial(c)
    return out


def type_maximum_likelihood(counts: Tuple[int, ...]) -> float:
    """max_theta p_theta(x) for any string x of the given type.

    The maximiser is the empirical distribution theta_i = n_i / n, giving
    prod_i (n_i/n)^{n_i}.
    """
    n = sum(counts)
    if n == 0:
        return 1.0
    value = 1.0
    for c in counts:
        if c:
            value *= (c / n) ** c
    return value


def shtarkov_sum_memoryless(alphabet_size: int, n: int) -> float:
    """C_S of the memoryless class over an alphabet of size `alphabet_size`.

    Complexity: O(n^{a-1}) types, each processed in O(a) time, so
    O(a * n^{a-1}) arithmetic operations -- exponentially better than the
    O(a^n) naive sum over messages, and the reason the price is computable
    at all for realistic block lengths in small alphabets.
    """
    total = 0.0
    for counts in compositions(n, alphabet_size):
        total += multinomial(counts) * type_maximum_likelihood(counts)
    return total


def price_bits(alphabet_size: int, n: int) -> float:
    """The exact price of universality, log2 C_S, in bits."""
    return math.log2(shtarkov_sum_memoryless(alphabet_size, n))


def rissanen_prediction(alphabet_size: int, n: int) -> float:
    """The conjectured asymptotic form ((a-1)/2) log2 n + Shtarkov's constant."""
    a = alphabet_size
    const = (math.log2(math.gamma(0.5) ** a / math.gamma(a / 2))
             + (a - 1) / 2 * math.log2(1 / (2 * math.pi)))
    return (a - 1) / 2 * math.log2(n) + const


def upper_bound_bits(alphabet_size: int, n: int) -> float:
    """The proved counting bound: C_S <= (n+1)^a, i.e. price <= a log2(n+1)."""
    return alphabet_size * math.log2(n + 1)

The average-case theory says: for a prior w on the class, the mixture
m_w = sum_theta w_theta p_theta is the Bayes-optimal code, and no code has
average redundancy below the capacity functional

    I(w) = sum_theta w_theta D(p_theta || m_w)   (bits).

Maximising I(w) over priors gives the redundancy-capacity lower bound
sup_w I(w) <= inf_q sup_theta D(p_theta || q), which is itself at most the
worst-case price log2 C_S.  The maximisation is exactly the channel-capacity
problem for the channel theta -> x with transition matrix p_theta(x), and is
solved by the Blahut--Arimoto alternating-maximisation iteration.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List, Sequence


def kl_bits(p: Sequence[float], q: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Relative entropy D(p||q) in bits, for positive probability vectors."""
    return sum(pi * math.log2(pi / qi) for pi, qi in zip(p, q) if pi > 0.0)


def mixture(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], w: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """The Bayes mixture m_w(x) = sum_theta w_theta p_theta(x)."""
    n_x = len(probs[0])
    return [sum(w[t] * probs[t][x] for t in range(len(probs))) for x in range(n_x)]


def mutual_information(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]], w: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """I(w) = sum_theta w_theta D(p_theta || m_w), in bits."""
    m = mixture(probs, w)
    return sum(w[t] * kl_bits(probs[t], m) for t in range(len(probs)) if w[t] > 0.0)


def shtarkov_sum(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> float:
    """C_S = sum_x max_theta p_theta(x) for a finite class given as a table."""
    return sum(max(row[x] for row in probs) for x in range(len(probs[0])))


def blahut_arimoto(probs: Sequence[Sequence[float]],
                   tol: float = 1e-12,
                   max_iter: int = 10_000) -> tuple[List[float], float]:
    """Maximise I(w) over priors by alternating maximisation.

    Iteration:  w'_theta  proportional to  w_theta * 2^{D(p_theta || m_w)}.
    Each sweep costs O(|Theta| * |X|); the iteration converges monotonically
    to the capacity, with the standard stopping certificate

        max_theta D(p_theta || m_w)  -  I(w)  <=  tol,

    which sandwiches the capacity between I(w) and I(w) + tol.
    """
    n_theta = len(probs)
    w = [1.0 / n_theta] * n_theta
    for _ in range(max_iter):
        m = mixture(probs, w)
        divergences = [kl_bits(probs[t], m) for t in range(n_theta)]
        gap = max(divergences) - sum(w[t] * divergences[t] for t in range(n_theta))
        if gap <= tol:
            break
        weights = [w[t] * (2.0 ** divergences[t]) for t in range(n_theta)]
        total = sum(weights)
        w = [x / total for x in weights]
    return w, mutual_information(probs, w)

// ---------- numerics ----------
function lgamma(x){ // Lanczos
  const g=7, c=[0.99999999999980993,676.5203681218851,-1259.1392167224028,
    771.32342877765313,-176.61502916214059,12.507343278686905,
    -0.13857109526572012,9.9843695780195716e-6,1.5056327351493116e-7];
  if(x<0.5) return Math.log(Math.PI/Math.sin(Math.PI*x))-lgamma(1-x);
  x-=1; let a=c[0]; const t=x+g+0.5;
  for(let i=1;i<g+2;i++) a+=c[i]/(x+i);
  return 0.5*Math.log(2*Math.PI)+(x+0.5)*Math.log(t)-t+Math.log(a);
}
function logBinom(n,k){ return lgamma(n+1)-lgamma(k+1)-lgamma(n-k+1); }

// contribution of the binary type with k ones
function typeTerm(n,k){
  if(k===0||k===n) return 1;
  return Math.exp(logBinom(n,k)+k*Math.log(k/n)+(n-k)*Math.log((n-k)/n));
}
function shtarkovBinary(n){
  let s=0; for(let k=0;k<=n;k++) s+=typeTerm(n,k); return s;
}
// general alphabet: sum over the type lattice
function shtarkovMemoryless(a,n){
  if(a===2) return shtarkovBinary(n);
  let total=0;
  const counts=new Array(a).fill(0);
  (function rec(i,left){
    if(i===a-1){
      counts[i]=left;
      let logm=lgamma(n+1), ml=0;
      for(let j=0;j<a;j++){ logm-=lgamma(counts[j]+1);
        if(counts[j]>0) ml+=counts[j]*Math.log(counts[j]/n); }
      total+=Math.exp(logm+ml);
      return;
    }
    for(let c=0;c<=left;c++){ counts[i]=c; rec(i+1,left-c); }
  })(0,n);
  return total;
}

  "interactive_layout": "# The Price of Universality

### One decompressor must serve every file. What does that cost?

Every archive you have ever opened was unpacked by a program that had never seen your file
before. That convenience — one shared decompressor, all possible inputs — cannot be free.
This page builds, from scratch, the exact accounting of what it costs, and answers a
practical question with a sharp theorem: **is it worth shipping a decompressor specialised
to your kind of data?**

By the end you will be able to state, and see for yourself, the following: the price is a
single number attached to your source model, it is about $\tfrac12\log_2 n$ bits per
unknown parameter on a message of length $n$, and it is *exactly* $n$ bits — that is,
everything — for a model rich enough to describe every individual file.

---

## 1. The setup, in one paragraph

Fix a finite set $X$ of possible messages, say all $n$-bit files. A *source* is a
probability distribution $p$ on $X$, and the ideal cost of encoding the message $x$ when
$p$ is known is $\log_2\frac{1}{p(x)}$ bits. A real code assigns integer lengths $\ell(x)$,
subject only to **Kraft's inequality** $\sum_x 2^{-\ell(x)}\le 1$, which is precisely the
condition for a prefix-free code with those lengths to exist. A universal scheme does not
know $p$; it knows only that $p$ lies in a family $\{p_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta}$. Its
**pointwise redundancy** is how much worse it does than the ideal code for the true source,
in the worst case over sources and messages:

$$\sup_\theta\sup_x\Big(\ell(x)-\log_2\tfrac{1}{p_\theta(x)}\Big).$$

<details>
<summary><b>New to source coding?</b> Click for the 60-second background</summary>

Shannon's source coding theorem says that a source $p$ cannot be compressed below its
entropy $H(p)=\sum_x p(x)\log_2\frac1{p(x)}$ bits per message on average, and that the
"ideal codeword length" $\log_2\frac{1}{p(x)}$ achieves it. Kraft's inequality is the
combinatorial constraint that makes codes finite objects: if you want short codewords for
some messages you must accept longer ones elsewhere, because the codewords must not be
prefixes of one another. Everything on this page is an accounting of the mismatch between
the code you can build (knowing only a family) and the code you would have built (knowing
the truth). A good entry point is
[Shannon's source coding theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannon%27s_source_coding_theorem)
and [Kraft's inequality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraft%E2%80%93McMillan_inequality).
</details>

---

## 2. The answer is a single number

Here is the whole theory in one definition. For each message, take the best any member of
the family can do for it, and add up:

$$C_S=\sum_{x\in X}\ \sup_{\theta\in\Theta} p_\theta(x).$$

This is the **Shtarkov sum**. Each source has total mass $1$; taking a pointwise maximum
over many sources produces something with mass more than $1$, and the excess *is* the
redundancy.

> **Theorem (exact minimax redundancy).** The price of universality of the family is
> $\log_2 C_S$ bits, up to one bit of integer rounding. The **normalized maximum
> likelihood** distribution $q^\star(x)=\sup_\theta p_\theta(x)/C_S$ satisfies
> $p_\theta(x)\le C_S\,q^\star(x)$ for all $\theta$ and $x$, so its code loses at most
> $\log_2 C_S+1$ bits against the true source on *every* message; and conversely every
> Kraft-compliant code has some message and some source on which it loses at least
> $\log_2 C_S$ bits.

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal both proofs — they are three lines each</summary>

**Achievability.** $q^\star$ is a probability distribution because we divided the envelope
by its own total mass. By construction $C_Sq^\star(x)=\sup_\theta p_\theta(x)\ge
p_\theta(x)$, so $\log_2\frac{1}{q^\star(x)}\le\log_2\frac{1}{p_\theta(x)}+\log_2C_S$;
rounding up to an integer costs less than one further bit.

**Converse.** Suppose a code $\ell$ beat the bound everywhere, i.e.
$2^{-\ell(x)}C_S>\sup_\theta p_\theta(x)$ for every $x$. Summing over all $x$ gives
$C_S\sum_x2^{-\ell(x)}>C_S$, so $\sum_x2^{-\ell(x)}>1$, contradicting Kraft. That is the
entire argument: a pigeonhole with weights.

Two consequences follow instantly. Always $C_S\ge1$ (universality never *helps*), and for a
finite family $C_S\le|\Theta|$ (you can always afford to name the source). If the family
contains a single source, $C_S=1$ and the price is exactly zero.
</details>

So everything reduces to: **how big is $C_S$?**

## 4. Why parametric models are cheap: the method of types

The families used in practice have infinitely many parameters, so "just name the source" is
useless. What saves us is that the likelihood usually depends on the message only through a
small summary.

> **Theorem (sufficient statistic).** If there is a map $T:X\to\sigma$ into a finite set
> such that $p_\theta(x)$ depends on $x$ only through $T(x)$, then $C_S\le|\sigma|$.

<details>
<summary>Click for the counting argument (it is genuinely pretty)</summary>

Fix a value $s$ and look at its fibre $F=\{x:T(x)=s\}$, of size $k$. On $F$ the maximum
likelihood is a single number $M$, because every source assigns the same probability to all
members of $F$. But each source spreads total mass at most $1$ over $F$ and does so evenly,
so each member gets at most $1/k$; hence $M\le1/k$ and the fibre contributes
$kM\le1$ to $C_S$. There are $|\sigma|$ fibres, and they partition $X$. $\blacksquare$
</details>

For a **memoryless source** over an alphabet $A$ producing $n$ symbols, the likelihood
$\prod_i\theta(x_i)$ depends only on the symbol counts, each in $\{0,\dots,n\}$:

$$C_S\le(n+1)^{|A|},\qquad\text{and in the binary case } C_S\le n+1 .$$

For a **first-order Markov chain**, the likelihood
$\nu(x_0)\prod_j T(x_j,x_{j+1})$ depends only on the first symbol and the matrix of
transition counts:

$$C_S\le|A|\,(n+1)^{|A|^2}.$$

In bits: a universal code is within $|A|\log_2(n+1)+1$ bits (memoryless) or
$\log_2|A|+|A|^2\log_2(n+1)+1$ bits (Markov) of the code tuned to the true source, on
*every* message. Divide by $n$: the per-symbol price tends to zero. **Universality is
asymptotically free per symbol.**

## 5. But it is not free: the $\tfrac12\log_2 n$ floor

An upper bound alone might mean the truth is zero. It is not. For a binary string with $k$
ones, the best any Bernoulli source can do is achieved at the empirical bias $k/n$, giving
maximum likelihood $(k/n)^k((n-k)/n)^{n-k}$, and all $\binom nk$ strings of that type share
it. So

$$C_S=\sum_{k=0}^n\binom nk\Big(\frac kn\Big)^k\Big(\frac{n-k}{n}\Big)^{n-k}.$$

> **Lemma (every interior type is heavy).** For $1\le k\le n-1$, each term above is at
> least $\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt n}$.

<details>
<summary>Click to reveal the two-sided Stirling proof, with explicit constants</summary>

Write $j=n-k$ and expand $\binom nk=n!/(k!\,j!)$. The powers of $e$ and of $n$ cancel
exactly, leaving

$$\binom nk\Big(\frac kn\Big)^k\Big(\frac jn\Big)^j=\frac{n!}{(n/e)^n}\cdot\frac{(k/e)^k}{k!}\cdot\frac{(j/e)^j}{j!}.$$

Now use Stirling from both sides: $m!\ge\sqrt{2\pi m}(m/e)^m$ bounds the first factor below
by $\sqrt{2\pi n}$, and $m!\le e\sqrt m\,(m/e)^m$ (valid for $m\ge1$) bounds the second and
third below by $1/(e\sqrt k)$ and $1/(e\sqrt j)$. So the product is at least
$\sqrt{2\pi n}/(e^2\sqrt{kj})$. Finally $\sqrt{kj}\le n/2$ by AM–GM, and numerically
$\sqrt{2\pi}>2.5$, $e^2<7.4$, so the bound is at least
$\frac{2.5\sqrt n}{7.4\,n/2}=\frac{5}{7.4\sqrt n}\ge\frac{1}{2\sqrt n}$. $\blacksquare$
</details>

Summing the $n-1$ interior types and throwing away the two extremes:

$$C_S\ \ge\ \frac{n-1}{2\sqrt n}\ \ge\ \frac{\sqrt n}{4}\qquad(n\ge2),$$

so the price is at least $\tfrac12\log_2 n-2$ bits. Together with the counting bound:

> **Theorem (the sandwich).** For the binary memoryless class and $n\ge2$,
> $$\tfrac12\log_2 n-2\ \le\ \log_2 C_S\ \le\ \log_2(n+1).$$

This is the classical parametric redundancy rate $\tfrac d2\log_2 n$ at $d=1$: real, but
only logarithmic. On a one-megabyte file, about eleven bits.

## 7. The other extreme: when specialisation buys nothing

Now push specialisation to its limit: allow **one decompressor per file**. Formally, the
family of point masses $\{\delta_y\}_{y\in X}$, where $\delta_y$ produces the file $y$ with
certainty and encodes it in zero bits. Compute the Shtarkov sum: for each $x$,
$\sup_y\delta_y(x)=1$, hence

$$C_S=\sum_{x\in X}1=|X|=2^n .$$

> **Theorem (separation).** On $n$-bit files with $n\ge2$, the memoryless class costs
> between $\tfrac12\log_2 n-2$ and $\log_2(n+1)$ bits, while the class of one source per
> file costs **exactly $n$ bits**.

Exactly $n$: the universal scheme facing that family is no better than storing the file
verbatim. The $n$ bits each specialist saved on its own file are precisely the $n$ bits the
universal scheme must spend saying which specialist to use. Nothing moved.

{{visualization:0}}

## 8. Why: the structural laws

Why does one shared parameter cost $\log n$ while a free choice per file costs $n$? Because
of how the price composes.

| law | statement | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| calibration | one-source family has $C_S=1$ | zero price when there is nothing to be uncertain about |
| monotonicity | enlarging a family cannot decrease $C_S$ | price measures class complexity |
| additivity | independent blocks: $C_S=C_S^{(1)}C_S^{(2)}$ | re-choosing parameters costs linearly |
| subadditivity | shared parameter: $C_S\le C_S^{(1)}C_S^{(2)}$ | **sharing is where the savings come from** |

<details>
<summary>Click for the one-line proofs</summary>

For an independent product the supremum over $(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ of
$p_{\theta_1}(x_1)p_{\theta_2}(x_2)$ factorises, and so does the double sum — hence exact
multiplicativity. For a tied product a single $\theta$ must serve both factors, so the
supremum is at most the product of the separate suprema — hence submultiplicativity, and
the slack is precisely the benefit of sharing. Applying the tied bound to a message split
into two blocks gives $C_S(n_1+n_2)\le C_S(n_1)C_S(n_2)$ for the memoryless class, so
$\log_2C_S(n)$ is subadditive and $\log_2C_S(n)/n$ converges by
[Fekete's lemma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subadditivity) — to zero, by the counting
bound.
</details>

## 9. The dual view: redundancy is a channel capacity

There is a second route to the same number, from information theory rather than counting.
Put a prior $w$ on the family, let $m_w=\sum_\theta w_\theta p_\theta$ be the mixture, and
recall relative entropy $D(p\|q)=\sum_x p(x)\log_2\frac{p(x)}{q(x)}$. Then, for any coding
distribution $q$, an exact algebraic identity holds:

$$\sum_\theta w_\theta D(p_\theta\|q)\;=\;I(w)\;+\;D(m_w\|q),\qquad
I(w)=\sum_\theta w_\theta D(p_\theta\|m_w).$$

Since $D\ge0$ (Gibbs), the mixture code is Bayes optimal and no code has average redundancy
below the **capacity** $I(w)$ — the mutual information between the unknown parameter and the
data. Moreover $I(w)\le\log_2C_S$ and $I(w)\le H(w)\le\log_2|\Theta|$: the average-case
theory sits below the worst-case theory, and neither exceeds the cost of naming the source.
Universal compression is, formally, the problem of learning which channel you are on while
using it.

## What to take away

**One number rules the problem.** The price of universality is $\log_2C_S$, the total mass
of the pointwise best-fit envelope of your source family.

**Structure is cheap; freedom is not.** A $d$-parameter family costs about
$\tfrac d2\log_2 n$ bits — provably between $\tfrac12\log_2n-2$ and $\log_2(n+1)$ in the
binary memoryless case. A family that can name every file costs the whole file.

**The dividing line is sharing.** The price is additive when blocks pick parameters
independently and only subadditive when they share one. Every gain from specialisation
comes from a parameter being reused across the data. If your "specialised" model has as
many degrees of freedom as your data has bits, you have moved nothing — you have only
renamed the problem.

# The Price of Universality I: Shtarkov's exact minimax redundancy

Research thread *Compression Beyond the Pigeonhole Bound*, Phase A, Question 1:
**one shared decompressor must serve all inputs**.  The counting core
(`MachineLearning.PRNGCompressionCore`) shows that no code shortens all inputs.
This file asks the quantitative refinement: if the data is known to come from
*some* member of a class of sources `{p_θ}_{θ ∈ Θ}`, how many bits does a single
universal code lose against the code tailored to the true `θ`?

## Central Idea

For a coding distribution `q` the pointwise redundancy at message `x` under
source `θ` is `log₂ (p_θ x / q x)`.  The worst case over `x` and `θ` is governed
by the **Shtarkov sum**

`Cₛ = ∑ₓ sup_θ p_θ x`,

and the optimum is attained by the *normalized maximum likelihood* distribution
`nml x = (sup_θ p_θ x) / Cₛ`.  Both directions are proved here, in a
division-free multiplicative form that needs no positivity assumptions, and in
logarithmic (bit) form under the natural positivity hypotheses.

## Main Results

* `maxLik`, `shtarkovSum`, `nml` — the basic objects
* `one_le_shtarkovSum`, `shtarkovSum_le_card` — `1 ≤ Cₛ ≤ #Θ`
* `prob_le_shtarkovSum_mul_nml` — achievability: NML pays at most `log₂ Cₛ`
  uniformly over messages *and* sources
* `exists_subprob_ratio_ge` — converse: *every* coding sub-probability `q`
  suffers redundancy at least `log₂ Cₛ` somewhere
* `shtarkov_minimax` — the two combined: the minimax pointwise redundancy is
  exactly `log₂ Cₛ`
* `kraft_converse` — code-length form: every code obeying Kraft has a message on
  which it is `log₂ Cₛ` bits worse than the ideal code for the true source
* `nmlCodeLength_le` — a matching universal code within one bit
* `shtarkovSum_eq_card_of_disjoint_supports` — for classes of mutually singular
  sources the price of universality is exactly `log₂ #Θ`: nothing can be shared

## Application Keywords

universal compression, minimax redundancy, Shtarkov sum, normalized maximum
likelihood, Kraft inequality, price of universality
-/

import Mathlib

open Finset Real

namespace UniversalRedundancy

/-- A parametric class of sources on a finite message space `X`, indexed by `Θ`. -/
structure SourceClass (X : Type*) [Fintype X] (Θ : Type*) where
  /-- probability of message `x` under source `θ` -/
  prob : Θ → X → ℝ
  nonneg : ∀ θ x, 0 ≤ prob θ x
  sum_one : ∀ θ, ∑ x, prob θ x = 1

namespace SourceClass

variable {X : Type*} [Fintype X] {Θ : Type*} (S : SourceClass X Θ)

lemma prob_le_one (θ : Θ) (x : X) : S.prob θ x ≤ 1 := by
  rw [← S.sum_one θ]
  exact Finset.single_le_sum (fun i _ => S.nonneg θ i) (Finset.mem_univ x)

include S in
lemma univ_nonempty [Nonempty Θ] : (univ : Finset X).Nonempty := by
  rcases Finset.eq_empty_or_nonempty (univ : Finset X) with h | h
  · exfalso
    have := S.sum_one (Classical.arbitrary Θ)
    rw [h] at this
    simp at this
  · exact h

/-- The maximum-likelihood envelope of the class: `sup_θ p_θ x`. -/
noncomputable def maxLik (x : X) : ℝ := ⨆ θ, S.prob θ x

lemma bddAbove_prob (x : X) : BddAbove (Set.range fun θ => S.prob θ x) := by
  refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
  rintro _ ⟨θ, rfl⟩
  exact S.prob_le_one θ x

lemma le_maxLik (θ : Θ) (x : X) : S.prob θ x ≤ S.maxLik x :=
  le_ciSup (S.bddAbove_prob x) θ

lemma maxLik_le {x : X} {c : ℝ} [Nonempty Θ] (h : ∀ θ, S.prob θ x ≤ c) :
    S.maxLik x ≤ c := ciSup_le h

lemma maxLik_nonneg [Nonempty Θ] (x : X) : 0 ≤ S.maxLik x :=
  le_trans (S.nonneg (Classical.arbitrary Θ) x) (S.le_maxLik _ x)

lemma maxLik_le_one [Nonempty Θ] (x : X) : S.maxLik x ≤ 1 :=
  S.maxLik_le fun θ => S.prob_le_one θ x

/-- **Shtarkov sum** of the class: `Cₛ = ∑ₓ sup_θ p_θ x`. -/
noncomputable def shtarkovSum : ℝ := ∑ x, S.maxLik x

/-- The Shtarkov sum is at least `1`: universality never *helps*. -/
theorem one_le_shtarkovSum [Nonempty Θ] : 1 ≤ S.shtarkovSum := by
  have h := S.sum_one (Classical.arbitrary Θ)
  calc (1 : ℝ) = ∑ x, S.prob (Classical.arbitrary Θ) x := h.symm
    _ ≤ ∑ x, S.maxLik x := Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ => S.le_maxLik _ x
    _ = S.shtarkovSum := rfl

theorem shtarkovSum_pos [Nonempty Θ] : 0 < S.shtarkovSum :=
  lt_of_lt_of_le zero_lt_one S.one_le_shtarkovSum

/-- The price of universality never exceeds `log₂ #Θ` bits: `Cₛ ≤ #Θ`. -/
theorem shtarkovSum_le_card [Nonempty Θ] [Fintype Θ] :
    S.shtarkovSum ≤ (Fintype.card Θ : ℝ) := by
  have hstep : ∀ x : X, S.maxLik x ≤ ∑ θ : Θ, S.prob θ x := by
    intro x
    refine S.maxLik_le fun θ => ?_
    exact Finset.single_le_sum (f := fun θ => S.prob θ x)
      (fun i _ => S.nonneg i x) (Finset.mem_univ θ)
  calc S.shtarkovSum ≤ ∑ x : X, ∑ θ : Θ, S.prob θ x :=
        Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ => hstep x
    _ = ∑ θ : Θ, ∑ x : X, S.prob θ x := Finset.sum_comm
    _ = ∑ _θ : Θ, (1 : ℝ) := by simp [S.sum_one]
    _ = (Fintype.card Θ : ℝ) := by simp

/-- The **normalized maximum likelihood** (Shtarkov) coding distribution. -/
noncomputable def nml (x : X) : ℝ := S.maxLik x / S.shtarkovSum

lemma nml_nonneg [Nonempty Θ] (x : X) : 0 ≤ S.nml x :=
  div_nonneg (S.maxLik_nonneg x) S.shtarkovSum_pos.le

lemma nml_sum_one [Nonempty Θ] : ∑ x, S.nml x = 1 := by
  unfold nml
  rw [← Finset.sum_div]
  exact div_self S.shtarkovSum_pos.ne'

/-- **Achievability.**  Under the NML distribution every source `θ` and every
message `x` incur redundancy at most `log₂ Cₛ`. -/
theorem prob_le_shtarkovSum_mul_nml [Nonempty Θ] (θ : Θ) (x : X) :
    S.prob θ x ≤ S.shtarkovSum * S.nml x := by
  unfold nml
  rw [mul_div_cancel₀ _ S.shtarkovSum_pos.ne']
  exact S.le_maxLik θ x

/-- **Converse.**  For any coding sub-probability `q` (in particular for the
implicit distribution `2 ^ (-ℓ x)` of any Kraft-compliant code) there is a
message where the maximum likelihood beats `q` by the factor `Cₛ`. -/
theorem exists_subprob_ratio_ge [Nonempty Θ] (q : X → ℝ) (hq : ∑ x, q x ≤ 1) :
    ∃ x, q x * S.shtarkovSum ≤ S.maxLik x := by
  by_contra hcon
  push_neg at hcon
  have hlt : ∑ x, S.maxLik x < ∑ x, q x * S.shtarkovSum :=
    Finset.sum_lt_sum_of_nonempty S.univ_nonempty fun x _ => hcon x
  have h2 : ∑ x, q x * S.shtarkovSum = (∑ x, q x) * S.shtarkovSum := by
    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
  have h3 : (∑ x, q x) * S.shtarkovSum ≤ S.shtarkovSum := by
    nlinarith [S.shtarkovSum_pos]
  have hcontra : S.shtarkovSum < S.shtarkovSum := by
    calc S.shtarkovSum = ∑ x, S.maxLik x := rfl
      _ < ∑ x, q x * S.shtarkovSum := hlt
      _ = (∑ x, q x) * S.shtarkovSum := h2
      _ ≤ S.shtarkovSum := h3
  exact absurd hcontra (lt_irrefl _)

/-- Converse, with an explicit witnessing source, for a finite class. -/
theorem exists_source_ratio_ge [Nonempty Θ] [Fintype Θ] (q : X → ℝ)
    (hq : ∑ x, q x ≤ 1) : ∃ x θ, q x * S.shtarkovSum ≤ S.prob θ x := by
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := S.exists_subprob_ratio_ge q hq
  obtain ⟨θ, hθ⟩ : ∃ θ : Θ, S.maxLik x = S.prob θ x := by
    obtain ⟨θ, hθ⟩ := Finite.exists_max fun θ : Θ => S.prob θ x
    exact ⟨θ, le_antisymm (S.maxLik_le fun θ' => hθ θ') (S.le_maxLik θ x)⟩
  exact ⟨x, θ, hθ ▸ hx⟩

/-- **Shtarkov's minimax theorem** (multiplicative form).  The constant `Cₛ` is
simultaneously achievable by one universal distribution and unavoidable for
every coding sub-probability: it *is* the minimax pointwise redundancy factor. -/
theorem shtarkov_minimax [Nonempty Θ] :
    (∀ θ x, S.prob θ x ≤ S.shtarkovSum * S.nml x) ∧
      (∀ q : X → ℝ, (∀ x, 0 ≤ q x) → ∑ x, q x ≤ 1 →
        ∀ c : ℝ, (∀ θ x, S.prob θ x ≤ c * q x) → S.shtarkovSum ≤ c) := by
  refine ⟨S.prob_le_shtarkovSum_mul_nml, ?_⟩
  intro q hq0 hq c hc
  have hmax : ∀ x, S.maxLik x ≤ c * q x := fun x => S.maxLik_le fun θ => hc θ x
  have hsum_nonneg : 0 ≤ ∑ x, q x := Finset.sum_nonneg fun x _ => hq0 x
  have key : S.shtarkovSum ≤ c * ∑ x, q x := by
    calc S.shtarkovSum = ∑ x, S.maxLik x := rfl
      _ ≤ ∑ x, c * q x := Finset.sum_le_sum fun x _ => hmax x
      _ = c * ∑ x, q x := by rw [Finset.mul_sum]
  have hone := S.one_le_shtarkovSum
  have hcpos : 0 < c := by nlinarith
  calc S.shtarkovSum ≤ c * ∑ x, q x := key
    _ ≤ c * 1 := by nlinarith
    _ = c := mul_one c

/-! ## Code-length form

A code with lengths `ℓ : X → ℕ` is *Kraft compliant* if `∑ₓ 2 ^ (-ℓ x) ≤ 1`;
this is exactly the condition for a prefix-free binary code to exist.  The ideal
code for a known source `θ` spends `log₂ (1 / p_θ x)` bits on `x`. -/

/-- Kraft compliance of a length function. -/
def Kraft (ℓ : X → ℕ) : Prop := ∑ x, (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(ℓ x : ℤ)) ≤ 1

/-- **Every** Kraft-compliant code overshoots the ideal code length of the true
source by at least `log₂ Cₛ` bits somewhere: multiplicative form
`2 ^ ℓ x * p_θ x ≥ Cₛ`. -/
theorem kraft_converse [Nonempty Θ] [Fintype Θ] (ℓ : X → ℕ) (h : Kraft ℓ) :
    ∃ x θ, S.shtarkovSum ≤ (2 : ℝ) ^ (ℓ x) * S.prob θ x := by
  obtain ⟨x, θ, hx⟩ := S.exists_source_ratio_ge (fun x => (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(ℓ x : ℤ))) h
  refine ⟨x, θ, ?_⟩
  have hpow : (0 : ℝ) < (2 : ℝ) ^ (ℓ x) := by positivity
  have hinv : (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(ℓ x : ℤ)) = ((2 : ℝ) ^ (ℓ x))⁻¹ := by
    rw [zpow_neg, zpow_natCast]
  rw [hinv, inv_mul_eq_div, div_le_iff₀ hpow] at hx
  calc S.shtarkovSum ≤ S.prob θ x * 2 ^ (ℓ x) := hx
    _ = (2 : ℝ) ^ (ℓ x) * S.prob θ x := by ring

lemma logb_two_pow (k : ℕ) : logb 2 ((2 : ℝ) ^ k) = (k : ℝ) := by
  rw [Real.logb_pow, Real.logb_self_eq_one (by norm_num)]
  ring

/-- Bit form of the converse: with positive probabilities, some message costs at
least `log₂ (1 / p_θ x) + log₂ Cₛ` bits. -/
theorem kraft_converse_bits [Nonempty Θ] [Fintype Θ] (ℓ : X → ℕ) (h : Kraft ℓ)
    (hpos : ∀ θ x, 0 < S.prob θ x) :
    ∃ x θ, logb 2 (1 / S.prob θ x) + logb 2 S.shtarkovSum ≤ (ℓ x : ℝ) := by
  obtain ⟨x, θ, hx⟩ := S.kraft_converse ℓ h
  refine ⟨x, θ, ?_⟩
  have hp := hpos θ x
  have h1 : logb 2 S.shtarkovSum ≤ logb 2 ((2 : ℝ) ^ (ℓ x) * S.prob θ x) :=
    Real.logb_le_logb_of_le (by norm_num) S.shtarkovSum_pos hx
  rw [logb_mul (by positivity) hp.ne', logb_two_pow] at h1
  have h3 : logb 2 (1 / S.prob θ x) = -logb 2 (S.prob θ x) := by
    rw [one_div, logb_inv]

open Finset Real

namespace UniversalRedundancy

variable {X : Type*} [Fintype X] {Θ : Type*} [Fintype Θ] [Nonempty Θ]

/-- Relative entropy (Kullback–Leibler divergence) measured in bits. -/
noncomputable def KLb (p q : X → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ x, p x * logb 2 (p x / q x)

/-- Shannon entropy in bits. -/
noncomputable def entropyb (p : X → ℝ) : ℝ := ∑ x, -(p x * logb 2 (p x))

/-- **Gibbs' inequality.**  Relative entropy between probability vectors with
positive entries is non-negative. -/
theorem KLb_nonneg (p q : X → ℝ) (hp : ∀ x, 0 < p x) (hq : ∀ x, 0 < q x)

      have hqx := hq x
      have hlt : Real.log (q x / p x) ≤ q x / p x - 1 :=

    intro x
    have hpx := hp x
    have hqx := hq x

noncomputable def mixture (S : SourceClass X Θ) (w : Θ → ℝ) (x : X) : ℝ :=
  ∑ θ, w θ * S.prob θ x

/-- The mutual information (capacity functional) of a prior. -/
noncomputable def mutualInfo (S : SourceClass X Θ) (w : Θ → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ θ, w θ * KLb (S.prob θ) (mixture S w)

/-- The Bayes-average redundancy of a coding distribution `q` under prior `w`. -/
noncomputable def bayesRedundancy (S : SourceClass X Θ) (w : Θ → ℝ) (q : X → ℝ) : ℝ :=

variable (S : SourceClass X Θ)

lemma mixture_pos (w : Θ → ℝ) (hw : ∀ θ, 0 < w θ) (hp : ∀ θ x, 0 < S.prob θ x) (x : X) :

  refine Finset.sum_pos (fun θ _ => mul_pos (hw θ) (hp θ x)) ⟨Classical.arbitrary Θ, mem_univ _⟩

        Finset.sum_congr rfl fun θ _ => by rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    _ = ∑ θ, w θ := by simp [S.sum_one]
    _ = 1 := hws

theorem compensation_identity (w : Θ → ℝ) (q : X → ℝ) (hw : ∀ θ, 0 < w θ)

theorem mutualInfo_le_bayesRedundancy (w : Θ → ℝ) (q : X → ℝ) (hw : ∀ θ, 0 < w θ)

  linarith

    rw [← Finset.sum_mul, hws, one_mul]

  linarith

The likelihood of a Markov chain factors as

`p_θ(x) = ν(x₀) · ∏_{j<n} T(x_j, x_{j+1})`,

counts*.  That is a statistic with at most `#A · (n+1)^(#A·#A)` values, and the
abstract counting theorem `shtarkovSum_le_of_product_form` converts this
directly into the redundancy bound

`Cₛ ≤ #A · (n+1)^(#A²)`,  i.e.  `price ≤ log₂ #A + #A² · log₂ (n+1)` bits.

* `markovChain_sum_one` — the Markov chain measure on `Aⁿ⁺¹` is normalized
  (proved by induction on `n`, propagating the initial law through the kernel)
* `markovClass` — the source class of first-order Markov chains
* `shtarkovSum_markovClass_le` — `Cₛ ≤ #A · (n+1)^(#A · #A)`

  `log₂ #A + #A² · log₂ (n+1) + 1` bits of the code tuned to the true chain,

through the kernel. -/
theorem markovChain_sum_one (trans : A → A → ℝ) (htrans : ∀ a, ∑ b, trans a b = 1) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (ν : A → ℝ), (∑ a, ν a = 1) →
      ∑ x : Fin (n + 1) → A, ν (x 0) * ∏ j : Fin n, trans (x j.castSucc) (x j.succ) = 1 := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      intro ν hν
      simp only [Finset.univ_eq_empty, Finset.prod_empty, mul_one]
      rw [← hν]
      exact Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.funUnique (Fin 1) A) _ _ fun x => rfl

        refine Fintype.sum_equiv (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ : Fin (k + 2) => A)).symm _ _

        rw [Fin.prod_univ_succ]

            = trans (x 0) (Fin.tail x 0) := by
          simp only [Fin.tail, Fin.castSucc_zero]
        have hstep : ∀ i : Fin k,
            trans (x i.succ.castSucc) (x i.succ.succ)
              = trans (Fin.tail x i.castSucc) (Fin.tail x i.succ) := by
          intro i
          simp only [Fin.tail, Fin.succ_castSucc]
        rw [h0, Finset.prod_congr rfl fun i _ => hstep i]

        rw [Finset.sum_comm]

          _ = ∑ a : A, ν a := by simp [htrans]
          _ = 1 := hν

  {θ : (A → ℝ) × (A → A → ℝ) //

  · positivity
  · rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]; field_simp
  · positivity
  · rw [Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ, nsmul_eq_mul]; field_simp

  prob θ x := θ.1.1 (x 0) * ∏ j : Fin n, θ.1.2 (x j.castSucc) (x j.succ)

Two extreme classes on the same message space `Bits n = Fin n → Bool` of

  sandwiched between `½ log₂ n − 2` and `log₂ (n+1)` bits

  possible class, i.e. "a decompressor specialised to each individual file":
  here the price is exactly `n` bits (`price_deltaClass_bits`).

entirely by the *complexity of the class*, not by the length of the data: a
`d`-parameter class moves `Θ(log n)` bits, while a class rich enough to name
every file moves nothing at all — the `n` bits that a specialised decompressor
saves on its own file are exactly the `n` bits the universal scheme must spend
to say which decompressor was used.

* `deltaClass` — the class of deterministic (point-mass) sources
* `shtarkovSum_deltaClass` — `Cₛ = #X` exactly

  deterministic class costs exactly `n` bits
* `savings_fraction_tendsto_zero` — the fraction of the message that a
  memoryless-specialised decompressor can absorb tends to `0`

class complexity, universal coding, specialised decompressor, pigeonhole bound,
minimax redundancy separation

    SourceClass X X where
  prob θ x := if x = θ then 1 else 0
  nonneg θ x := by split <;> norm_num
  sum_one θ := by simp

shared: `Cₛ = #X`. -/

  unfold SourceClass.shtarkovSum
  rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => maxLik_deltaClass x]
  simp

redundancy of a source class was identified *exactly* with `log₂ Cₛ`, the log of
the Shtarkov sum.  Here we bound `Cₛ` for the classes that matter in practice —
memoryless (i.i.d.) sources and Markov sources — and obtain closed-form bounds
in the message length `n` and the *class complexity*.

## Central Idea

The abstract engine is a **sufficient statistic** bound: if the likelihood
`p_θ x` depends on `x` only through a statistic `T x` taking `N` values, then

`Cₛ ≤ N`.

Indeed the fibre of `T` over a value `s` has some cardinality `k`, on which the
maximum likelihood is a constant `M`; since `k · p_θ x ≤ 1` for every `θ`, also
`k · M ≤ 1`, so each fibre contributes at most `1` to `∑ₓ maxₜ p_θ x`.

For a class whose likelihood is a product of `m` factors drawn from a finite
"feature alphabet" `B` (times a factor depending on a finite initial statistic
in `C`), the counts of the features form such a statistic, giving

`Cₛ ≤ #C · (m+1) ^ #B`.

Specialising: memoryless sources over an alphabet `A` on messages of length `n`
give `Cₛ ≤ (n+1) ^ #A`, and first-order Markov sources give
`Cₛ ≤ #A · (n+1) ^ (#A · #A)`.  In bits: the price of universality is at most
`#A · log₂ (n+1)` resp. `log₂ #A + #A² · log₂ (n+1)` bits — logarithmic in `n`,
matching the Rissanen-style `(d/2) log₂ n` rate up to the constant factor `2`
in front of the parameter dimension `d`.

* `SourceClass.shtarkovSum_le_of_product_form` — counting bound for product

method of types, sufficient statistic, Rissanen redundancy, Markov sources,
universal coding, parametric class complexity

theorem shtarkovSum_le_card_statistic [Nonempty Θ] {σ : Type*} [Fintype σ]

    S.shtarkovSum ≤ (Fintype.card σ : ℝ) := by
  classical
  have hfib : ∀ s : σ, ∑ x ∈ univ.filter (fun x => T x = s), S.maxLik x ≤ 1 := by
    intro s
    rcases Finset.eq_empty_or_nonempty (univ.filter (fun x => T x = s)) with he | hne
    · simp [he]
    obtain ⟨x0, hx0⟩ := hne
    have hx0' : T x0 = s := (Finset.mem_filter.mp hx0).2
    have hconstprob : ∀ θ, ∀ x ∈ univ.filter (fun x => T x = s),
        S.prob θ x = S.prob θ x0 := by
      intro θ x hx
      exact hT θ x x0 (by rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp hx).2, hx0'])
    have hconst : ∀ x ∈ univ.filter (fun x => T x = s), S.maxLik x = S.maxLik x0 := by
      intro x hx
      unfold SourceClass.maxLik
      exact congrArg _ (funext fun θ => hconstprob θ x hx)
    set k : ℕ := (univ.filter (fun x => T x = s)).card with hk
    have hkpos : 0 < k := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨x0, hx0⟩
    have hmass : ∀ θ, (k : ℝ) * S.prob θ x0 ≤ 1 := by
      intro θ
      have h1 : ∑ x ∈ univ.filter (fun x => T x = s), S.prob θ x = (k : ℝ) * S.prob θ x0 := by
        rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl (hconstprob θ), Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hk]
      have h2 : ∑ x ∈ univ.filter (fun x => T x = s), S.prob θ x ≤ ∑ x, S.prob θ x :=

      rw [S.sum_one θ] at h2
      linarith [h1 ▸ h2]
    have hkR : (0 : ℝ) < (k : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hkpos
    have hmaxle : S.maxLik x0 ≤ 1 / (k : ℝ) := by
      refine S.maxLik_le fun θ => ?_

    _ ≤ ∑ _s : σ, (1 : ℝ) := Finset.sum_le_sum fun s _ => hfib s
